citations.claim: controller force exceeds fmax at first violating step
previous step force was clamped at limit

counterfactual.change: Reduced kp from 21.386 to 10.0 (single field) to lower raw velocity-error demand below fmax; with lower demand the missing clamp is not needed and controller_force stays within limit for same 334 steps.

explanation: Controller force exceeds fmax at step 334 (214.48 > 156.01) while previous steps were clamped exactly at fmax (156.01). The velocity-error law (kp * velocity error) computes a demand > fmax and the clamping/saturation is not applied correctly on that step — likely a missed clamp after sub-step splitting (substeps_in_step=2) or after accumulating correction. Lowering kp reduces the raw demand below fmax so the missing clamp is not exposed and no violation occurs.
vision_note: Between steps 331 and 334 the controller body (left, blue/orange) stays far from its green waypoint near the center while the small red violating body drifts only slightly downward beside the waypoint. No wall penetration, tunneling, large position jump or energy explosion is visible; motion is smooth and continuous across all four tiles with substep splitting not discernible.
